title: N Meetings in One Room
statement:
There is a single meeting room and `n` meeting requests. Meeting `i` starts at time `start[i]` and ends at time `end[i]`, with `start[i] ≤ end[i]`.

Only one meeting can use the room at a time, and the room is occupied during the whole closed interval `[start[i], end[i]]`. Therefore two chosen meetings are compatible only if the later one starts **strictly after** the earlier one ends; if one meeting ends at time `t`, the next may start at `t + 1` or later but not at `t`.

Choose a set of pairwise compatible meetings so that the number of meetings held is as large as possible, and print that number.

**Follow-up:** in the interview this was followed by a logic puzzle (three boxes labelled apples, oranges and apples-and-oranges, all labels wrong); it is not part of this task.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `start[i]` and `end[i]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum number of meetings that can be held.

examples.explanation: Take [1,3], then [4,6] (it starts after 3), then [9,10]. The meeting [6,8] cannot follow [4,6] because it starts at time 6, when the room is still in use. No selection of 4 meetings is compatible.
The two meetings at [5,5] clash with each other (same time), so at most one of them is held, followed by [6,7].
Skip the long meeting [0,10] and hold [1,2], [3,4] and [5,6].

hints: Which meeting should you hold first if you want to leave as much time as possible for the rest?
Sort the meetings by end time. Greedily take a meeting whenever it starts strictly after the end of the last meeting you took.
Remember that equal times conflict: compare with `>`, not `>=`.
